entry.title: Talking about the subconscious
entry.content:
So I’ve got an interesting topic this week.

Sometimes I get a kind of, theme? No actually, it’s more like a common element that keeps popping up. A theme is more like the “moral of the story” that things are revolving around. Rahhh anyways. I wanted to talk about the subconscious because it’s been cropping up in my life a lot recently.

Here are some examples:

  1. I’ve been getting back into magick and a common element of magick is using your subconscious in your favor.
  2. I’ve been noticing a pattern of self-hatred and self-loathing. I saw a video today by Dr. K titled “Why Self-Pity Can Feel So Good” that talks about the need for the subconscious to keep it’s mental model of the world consistent. Consistency trumps feeling good.
  3. I’ve been noticing that my cognitive, emotional, and other such “front of the mind” coping mechanisms failing or being inadequate as of recent. I’ve been trying to study and I tend to procrastinate or ruminate (see last weeks post). This is odd as I’m usually more on the ball, I think.

That being said, I’d like to write a bit on this to clear my head and maybe help my understanding of my situation. I’ve been trying to make changes in my life to help my study habits. I’ve had a bit of a break period recently and I’ve been trying to catch up on school and my hobbies. So far it’s not been the best. With school it feels like I’m pulling teeth to get anything done. As of now I’m assuming that’s because my strategy of school is intensity over consistency, not great but I’m trying to establish a routine of studying after work. It’s not perfect but since I work in the early mornings (5am is when I get up), studying in the mornings is probably more trouble than it’s worth.

Oh some good news, I got caught up in the course that’s been troubling me, Calculus 3. I’ve scored pretty low (50s and 40s) on the last 2 exams, but I’m hoping I can still bring it back. If not, it is what it is, I’ll try again next semester. I don’t want to drop the course, but I’ve got 3 weeks to decide if I need to. If I bomb the next exam or can’t recover to a B, I will unfortunately have to drop the course. It sucks too because I really like this class, I’ve just been in a rough period because I took too many classes this semester.

Anyways, around this whole thing with the subconcious. I’ve been trying to get myself studying by the old un-reliable method of being mean to myself in ways that are not helpful. That’s not something I’ve found a total solution for yet. Like I said I’ve tried the cognitive, emotional, and other such techniques. They all feel like band-aid fixes. They help a little in the moment but aren’t substantial enough. Also I can’t really go to therapy due to my busy lifestyle at the moment, so that’s out of the picture for now.

After watching a few videos on things involving the subconscious, magickal, therapeutic, or otherwise, I might’ve found a new lead. So, one thing I heard recently that stuck with me is that “You can’t argue or reason with your subconscious, you can only provide it different evidence.” And that makes a lot of sense. I mean you can’t tell someone to just love themselves. Even if they don’t consciously make an effort to be mean to themselves, and they can see the value of self-love, that’s not something in their direct control. It’s the subconscious mental model from lived experience that tells them “you are unlovable” or other things of that nature. So if my problem of self loathing, procrastination, and generally just being mean to myself is out of my direct cognitive or emotional control, then it’s probably under the control of my subconscious.

Okay… then what do we do? I reckon that if I can find an outline of what my mental model is like around the topic of self loathing and stuff, I can slowly but surely convince myself through real world experience of a different mental model.

So if the mental model I have causes me to respond with procrastination, rumination, self-loathing, and other stuff like that, then what is triggering that response? My first hypothesis is going to be something like:

Want to do something —> Compare where you’re at to where you want to be.
If Bad: Make yourself feel bad to get yourself working harder or to quit so you don’t have to do stuff that makes you feel bad anymore.
If Good: Move on to next thing.

Man, that’s rough lol. So if our mental model is causing us to do a comparison and either feel bad or move on, then there’s no wonder why this cycle is so vicious. We have our inputs and outputs tho, we don’t neccesarily need the internal logic of this system but a rough guess would be nice.

Hmm…. So my subconscious has a behavior^ that probably comes from some belief. What is that belief? ‘Something is only worth doing if we’re good at it’ Maybe not that. ‘If you’re bad at something you care about, you should feel bad about that.’ Okay well obviously that’s not true, but that seems pretty accurate. Well, why is this belief there? It’s probably there to save me from some perceived threat. Maybe it’s the threat of hard things being stressful. Probably but that’s likely not it. I think it’s a mixture of saving me from wasting my time with ‘useless’ effort, and to motivate me to do better. It’s trying to get me away from the bad feeling by either working hard or quitting. Well even when I work hard the feeling is still there, usually it actually gets worse. I’m going to assume this is a faulty/unintended response.

So my subconscious says “If you’re bad at something you care about, you should feel bad about that,” likely to get me to work harder or to quit and save my energy. Well, what’s another belief that doesn’t make me feel bad but still gets me to work hard when I’m bad at something? “If you’re bad you need to work harder.” Well that’s not gonna work, besides I already feel that way usually. “If you fail, try something different.” I think that’s already there too, it’s also not quite what I’m looking for. One belief that I don’t see is that “hard work always pays off,” as I’m very lazy if I let myself be.

I think my brain has a like, messed up relationship between what I enjoy and how I do at said thing. What can I do to prove to myself something to replace that previous belief. The problem is mainly the hatred, procrastination, self loathing, all that is really bad for problem solving and my health. What am I afraid of believing? I think that’s a good place to go. “If you work hard and are patient, you will get what you are looking for.” You see that scares me.

I’m someone who believes very much so in materialism, peoples circumstances can determine a lot about their life. But in recent months I’ve been trying to meld the ideas of perennialism and spirtual things with materialist conceptions of the world. I’m someone who thinks for example, if God is good, then God will not smite you or send you to hell for believing in a different God. I also think something like, enlightment, is achievable by anyone. Not easily, and most will not achieve it in their current lifetime, but I think it is possible. Because, if I believe that some are not meant to reach peace and happiness, then that’s a level of cosmic injustice I couldn’t bear. I know there’s evil terrible things that happen out in the world, but I can’t bear the thought that there is genuinely no hope for some people.

I bring this up, because of the idealist and materialist tensions that in part cause me to fair that way of thinking. “If you work hard and are patient, you will be find what you’re looking for,” feels like it’s an indictment of people who are unhappy due to their material conditions. If you’re born with 1 arm and no legs in a poor country with little oppurtunity, does this imply that you ought to just work harder? How the hell are you supposed to pull yourself up by bootstraps that you can’t even afford nor physically reach? I know that spiritual peace and good material conditions are mutually dependent, but I’m worried if I take on that belief, I’ll start to look down on others who ‘haven’t worked hard enough’ and such. That also means, that I could have everything I want but I’m just not good enough.

So I’m gonna guess that’s not a good replacement belief, but I think I have a new idea. Something like ‘Better is possible.’ A sort of hope. But this doesn’t guide me at all how I am supposed to get to better. And overtime as I fail and the light starts to dim, that belief will become twisted as it has been up until now. There’s one belief I already have that I could try leaning into more. Something like ‘There’s always another option,’ or ‘there’s always a solution.’

My head is starting to hurt from all this, I’ll stop for now lol.

Wait before I go, maybe I can prove to my subconcious by repeated exposure that hard work ain’t so bad, and that progress is possible.

I’ll settle on that, progress is possible.

Thanks for reading this long ass rant post, hopefully the next one is a bit more concise. Bye!

entry.title: I don’t know what to write about tbh

link.title: I don’t know what to write about tbh

entry.content:
I’m not sure about what to write about.

Also, sorry about posting late, I know pretty much no one reads this but I try to keep things on schedule. But let me rephrase that first statement. It’s not that I don’t know “what” to write about, it’s more in what order, and what should I leave out?

Eh idk, it’s late. Here’s my stream of conciousness as per usual:

The last couple weeks have been hectic, (see the fact that I missed a post last week) and things are calming down, sort of??? I had a couple thoughts I wanted to share. My daily notes in obsidian are super bloated and essentially contain my entire schedule for the day, which is redundant as I have that in my calendar I regularly use and refer to. I set a rule for myself a day or two before realizing this that I’m only allowed to edit my daily template once every two weeks so in service of this, I have edited my calendar and have been rewriting each individual daily note instead of the template because I couldn’t take it anymore.

Now my day is divided by 3 categories: Obligations, Hangouts, & Endeavors. Obligations are things that don’t take much mental effort and generally require me just showing up on time. Examples of this are work, class, personal care like sleep, eating, showers, and other regularly scheduled events. Hangouts are, well fun hangouts. Social events and other things that aren’t neccesarily “obligatory” but I still really want to do. These are different mostly to distinguish what I can reschedule with little effort, at least compared to my obligations. Lastly we have, endeavors. Endeavors are things I choose to do that I’m committing to. It’s like an obligation but generally takes more effort than just simply showing up. Endeavors are also the primary place I choose to put tasks in now, BOOM! My daily note used to be filled with “tasks” that were really just placeholders for 80% obligations and hangouts. Since those are effectively removed, I only really have to worry about the things I choose to pursue for my own reasons. In this category is stuff like cleaning my room, going to the gym, studying x amount of material, playing guitar for t amount of time, etc. As you can likely see, I want to spend more of my time thinking about stuff like that, I want to prioritize my focus mainly around that. Before I’d see this giant list of “tasks” and be overwhelmed. Now I see my list of tasks and it’s basically all stuff I actually have to think about, which definitely removes a lot of that decision or ruminatively based fatigue.

Since only seeing endeavor related tasks, I now also realize how little time I have for myself throughout my days. I won’t bore y’all to death with sappy “I have a full time job and do college, woe is me” kind of stuff. I could, but I’m not always interested in stuff like that, especially when it’s not currently impeding my ability to tackle the problems in my life. But since I now realize how little time I have for myself, things feel different. I no longer have an entire day to do homework after work. I really only have 2-6 and sometimes MAYBE 8 hours. This gives me a better understanding of my situation, and recontextualizes my entire approach towards these sorts of things. It’s early days now, but I really think this will help me value the time I have in my life. I hope it helps me tackle these things to a suitable level.

Oh yeah, in consequence to this change of perspective, I’ve already realized something. I don’t have a consistent daily routine for my hobbies, and barely have one for studying. To fix this, I’m going to try and study for a little (5-30 minutes) bit each morning. I know it’s not going to move mountains, but this will help me keep my momentum (holy shit that’s a witty reference) and start my day off strong. On this same theme of small daily habits, I literally have nothing like that for my hobbies so I’m going to implement a small (also 5-30 minutes) daily hobby session at the end of the day before bed. I’m going to do that quite soon so I’ll have to wrap up shortly.

entry.title: Keeping your momentum is important!
entry.content:
This week has been interesting. I mostly want to talk about today though.

Today I studied a whole bunch on Calculus 3 with varying results. I’m a bit behind in this class as of right now. It’s not too bad so far, just things have been a little hard to keep up with due to my life being super busy. I got up and started studying around 9am. My original plan was to study from around 9am - 6pm. That would be a sum total of 9 hours if I was just studying. With breaks I thought probably more like 5-7 hours. Okay cool, well then I got started and everything went obviously according to plan.

At 11am I got distracted, I think I was doing a mixture of talking to my friends on the phone, family in the house, and trying to make breakfast. By about 2pm I finally got back on the horse again. At around 3pm again I felt stuck. Something was just not working. I took another break from 3pm-4pm.

At 5:30pm I began studying again, again 100% on schedule. At 6pm I realized it STILL wasn’t working. So I went and called a “friend” (you know who you are) and decided to give up on a problem that was giving me some trouble. By about 6:30pm I seemed to be getting somewhere. I thought, “I’ll just study till 7pm.” By 8pm I had to force myself to stop because I was doing so well.

So the main takeaways I got from this, other than I am very good at staying on schedule, is that I need to keep my momentum.

Oxford Dictionary defines momentum, probably, but I am not going to use their definition because that’s unhelpful. I’m defining momentum as the phenomenon where you’re doing something and it takes more effort to switch between things than it is to keep doing the same thing. You can call this inertia, resistance, habits, whatever, but I’ll be calling it momentum. It seems that at around 11am today I lost my momentum, attempted to restart my study session at 2pm and unfortunately ran into a huge momentum killer, to the point where I only really got it back at around 6pm.

The momentum killer, I suspect, was a particularly difficult homework problem about finding the vector parametrization of the intersection of 2 surfaces. I wrote it down somewhere but I don’t want to find it. I believe the problem killed my momentum not only because of the logic I’m proposing but also because this is a repeated phenomena. I have a tendency to stick it out on difficult homework problems, which can be helpful, but it can also be a hinderance. I’ve noticed myself stop my sessions frustrated most often because I kind of have a “thug it out” sort of mindset about these things. I really would like to get better at solving this problem I run into so often.

Anyways, I’m spending all these silly keystrokes to say that, you gotta conserve your momentum. I lost roughly 5 hours of an 11 hour total study session, and while that 11 hours isn’t healthy, it could’ve been much better if I had conserved my momentum. For future reference I’m gonna try and shelve super difficult problems whenever I hit them, and if I hit a few (say 3-5 ish ) in a row, I’ll slow down, take a break, come back and switch from the quick-minded mode I usually operate in to a more slow-and-steady approach that it takes to solve these difficult problems.

Hey that’s a good way of thinking of it. Speed vs Power. The difficult ones require much more power, and will require less over time which means more speed to keep me interested. Same thing with the easier problems. It might be that switching modes is what’s causing the momentum loss.

But yeah, I’ll shelve difficult problems to keep my momentum, and try to take it slower when solving those more difficult ones as to not burn myself out.

entry.title: Overcommitting
entry.content:
I have this weird habit of overcommitting to things.

Well actually no. I’m not going to change the title, but it’s like I get so attatched to certain ideas and since I’m kind of a scatterbrain, I get a lot of ideas that sound good. I try to do all of them and stretch myself thin in the process. As you can likely see, this blog post is 2 days late. This is another example of this phenomenon. I don’t really know what to do about it but I wanted to put out something for the week so, vent post?

You ever hear the phrase “Under promise, over deliver”? That’s probably written as an antithesis to me. I don’t like letting people down. I don’t like letting myself down. But to be frank, I don’t know what to do about the whole situation. There’s a loneliness to that. To trying, and failing, and trying and failing, and seeing the needle move ever so slightly, but falling back into place soon after. I’m tired.

entry.title: Considering regular blog posts
entry.content:
Hello all 👋, it’s been a minute.

School has been sort of kicking my ass again? It’s a bit hard to describe.

Like, I struggled with school for a long time because of my untreated ADHD, but now I’m still struggling while medicated.

The thing is though, I’m not really upset about the whole thing. It currently feels like every issue that pops up surrounding school has a suitable solution. There is no insurmountable barrier keeping me from solving my own problems. It’s like I have all the pieces needed, I just have to put them together in the right way. Very strange is what I’ll say, this feeling is very foreign.

Not unpleasant though, that’s nice.

Hmm, other updates I guess:

  • I’ve gotten to see a bunch of my friends recently, yay!
  • I’ve started a couple new things:
    • A sort of open research group, hopefully I’ll talk on this l8r.
    • A fortnightly hobby swap. (The current one is music creation, I hope to share something soon).
    • Oh and the topic of this blog post.

I am considering making weekly/fortnightly/monthly/regularly scheduled blog posts.

I’m not sure what about, but I know I could find something to write about once a week, even if it’s only for my emotional wellbeing.

One thing that encouraged me to do this was an idea of, ‘Jae’s Cool Thing of the (Insert-Time-Period-Here)’. I could find or make or at least share one thing I thought was neat every week. Hell I could even make a fun special heading for it or something (not yet though I’m lazy rn).

With that being said.

entry.title: Working on a process for writing song ideas

link.title: Working on a process for writing song ideas

entry.content:
Hey guys! Welcome to 2026!

This one’s gotta be another quick one but I’ve been working on this as of late. I often struggle with writing down song ideas as I have them, and this makes the process of music creation really difficult. To combat this, I’ve got a little method of writing down ideas now.

Basic Song Drafting:

  1. Rhythm + Tempo
  2. Melody + Harmony
  3. Song Structure

Intermediate Song Drafting:

  1. Timbre + Texture
  2. Dynamics + Articulation
  3. Style/Vibe

Advanced Song Drafting:

  1. Concept/Story/Narrative
  2. Song Write Up
  3. Lyrics if wanted

I’ll see how well this works and hopefully will do more with this soon. Bye for now!

And probably some other stuff I forgot to mention. Most of this stuff has been on the backburner for a long time, I’m really happy to finally go through with it!
